sections.h2: Which Newark office sends the property tax bill?
sections.html:
The City of Newark Department of Finance bills and collects it, and Essex County is the county that hears assessment appeals. Inside Finance, the Assessments unit decides what real estate is taxable, keeps a tax map for every parcel and records ownership and mortgage changes. Revenue Collections sends the bills, takes the payments and runs enforcement when taxes go unpaid.

To learn what a Newark property owes, call customer service Monday through Friday, 9 am to 4 pm, except holidays. The tax lines are 973-733-3791, 973-733-3792, 973-733-3962, 973-733-8098 and 973-733-3978. The city's Payment Center also takes online tax payments by credit card, debit card or electronic check.

sections.h2: When are Newark property taxes due?
sections.html:
Installments are due on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, the quarterly dates that apply across New Jersey. Late amounts can carry interest of up to 8 percent on the first $1,500 and up to 18 percent above that, plus a penalty of up to 6 percent for delinquencies above $10,000 when the fiscal year closes.

Newark applies a partial payment to the oldest quarter outstanding. A homeowner who owes the first three quarters and sends money in September sees it go against the first quarter's principal and interest, so the later quarters stay open. That matters for a seller, because the payoff on the closing statement can be larger than a quick tally of the latest bill suggests.

sections.h2: What happens to a Newark house when taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The city sells a tax lien certificate on it. Newark runs a standard tax sale for prior years' taxes and charges that are still owing, and an accelerated tax sale for the current year's charges that remain due after the statutory date of November 10. Its Finance page cites N.J.S.A. 54:5-19 for taxes outstanding from the prior year.

  • The buyer of the certificate holds a lien and does not take title at the auction.
  • A town holder can sue to foreclose six months after the sale, and a private holder can sue after two years.
  • An owner can demand in writing, before final judgment, that the property go to a sheriff's sale so any equity is protected.
  • Redemption stays open until the Superior Court enters a judgment barring it.

Our New Jersey tax sale guide covers redemption costs and the equity demand in detail.

sections.h2: Where do I file an appeal of a Newark assessment?
sections.html:
File with the Essex County Board of Taxation on Form A-1, together with the comparable sales form that goes with it. The petition must be filed and received by April 1, or by May 1 when a municipal revaluation or reassessment has been done. For a property assessed above $1,000,000, the owner may file directly with the State Tax Court instead.

The burden sits with the owner. You have to show that the assessed value is unreasonable compared with a market value standard. An assessment counts as excessive or discriminatory only if it fails both the true market value standard and the common level range, which is plus or minus 15 percent of the district's average ratio.

  • A judgment from the county board can be appealed to the Tax Court of New Jersey within 45 days.
  • An added or omitted assessment, which arises when changes are made to a property after October 1, is appealed on Form AA-1.
  • An added assessment above $750,000 in total may go directly to the Tax Court.

sections.h2: What does Newark look like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Puritans from the New Haven Colony settled Newark in 1666, and it became a city on April 11, 1836. It is the county seat of Essex County and New Jersey's largest city, with a Census Bureau estimate of 323,808 residents for July 2025 on 24.14 square miles of land. Most households rent, so a seller often deals with tenants already in the building. The city has five wards, and heavily industrial land around the airport and seaport sits mostly in the East and South wards, while homes cluster in the North, Central and West wards.

The land slopes from about 230 feet in the western section down to sea level in the east, in a basin that drains toward the Passaic River. Historically the higher ground, around Forest Hill, High Street and Weequahic, drew the wealthier families. The East Ward's Ironbound is a dense district of apartment buildings and rowhouses, while the marshes on Newark Bay were reclaimed in the 1920s for the airport and Port Newark.

sections.h2: Which Newark neighborhoods and roads shape a sale?
sections.html:
Each ward has its own housing mix. The North Ward is centered on Branch Brook Park and takes in Broadway, Mount Pleasant, Upper Roseville and Forest Hill, where the Forest Hill Historic District holds older mansions and colonial homes. The West Ward covers Vailsburg, Ivy Hill, the West Side, Fairmount and Lower Roseville. The South Ward includes Weequahic, Clinton Hill and Dayton, and the Central Ward holds University Heights and Government Center.

Newark is served by the New Jersey Turnpike (Interstate 95), Interstate 280, Interstate 78, the Garden State Parkway, U.S. Routes 1/9 and 22, and Route 21. Newark Penn Station, east of downtown, carries PATH, NJ Transit and Amtrak trains, and the Newark Light Rail links it to Broad Street Station. In 2020, 40.3 percent of Newark households had no car, so a short walk to transit is a real selling point for many buyers.

More than 100,000 people commute to Newark each workday, and nearly 50,000 students attend its universities and medical and law schools. Newark Public Schools is the largest school system in the state.

sections.h2: How should I handle tax due when I sell a Newark house?
sections.html:
Ask Revenue Collections for a written statement covering every unpaid quarter, interest and any tax sale certificate, dated to the closing day. Whoever handles the closing pays that balance from the seller's proceeds, which clears the lien for the buyer.

  • List every quarter that is open, including prior-year balances, since those can already be in a tax sale.
  • Check whether a certificate was sold and recorded, and who holds it.
  • If an assessment appeal is pending, tell your closing attorney so the filing is accounted for at closing.
  • Plan for the seller-paid realty transfer fee on the deed.

faqs.q: Who do I call to find out what I owe on a Newark house?
faqs.a: Call Newark's Finance customer service on a weekday between 9 am and 4 pm at 973-733-3791, one of five tax lines the city lists. Ask for the amount through your closing date.

faqs.q: By what date must a Newark assessment petition arrive?
faqs.a: The deadline is April 1, or May 1 if a revaluation or reassessment was done. File Form A-1 with the Essex County Board of Taxation. Owners of property assessed above $1,000,000 can go straight to the Tax Court.

faqs.q: What interest does Newark charge on late taxes?
faqs.a: Interest can reach 8 percent on the first $1,500 and 18 percent on the balance above that, under state law. A penalty of up to 6 percent can follow when the delinquency is over $10,000 at year end.

faqs.q: Does paying part of my bill stop a tax sale?
faqs.a: A partial payment is credited to the oldest quarter first, which cuts that quarter's principal and interest but leaves later quarters open. Newark can still sell a certificate for prior years' taxes that remain unpaid.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Newark house that has a tax sale certificate on it?
faqs.a: Yes. The certificate amount and its interest come out of the sale price at closing, and the holder then discharges the lien. Get the payoff from the tax collector in writing so the title company can wire the exact amount.
